title: Abraham
lead: The ancestor of Israel, called by God to leave Mesopotamia for Canaan with the promise of land, offspring and blessing for all nations. Jews, Christians and Muslims all honor him: the New Testament calls him the father of all who believe (Romans 4:11–16), and the Qur'an calls him God's friend (Qur'an 4:125).

sections.b: After Genesis 11–25, Abraham is remembered as the one God chose and called (Nehemiah 9:7–8), God's friend (2 Chronicles 20:7; Isaiah 41:8), and the rock from which Israel was cut (Isaiah 51:1–2). God names himself "the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:6), and Jesus uses that name to argue that the dead live to God (Mark 12:26–27). John the Baptist warns that being Abraham's children is not enough (Matthew 3:9), and Jesus speaks of the poor man carried to "Abraham's side" (Luke 16:22). Paul makes him the father of all who trust God, circumcised or not (Romans 4; Galatians 3), Hebrews makes him a model of faith (Hebrews 11:8–19), and James of faith shown in deeds (James 2:21–23).
